findings.evidence: Line 35 is now `variable (X : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]` (diff removes `[CompleteSpace X]`); `structure StronglyContinuousSemigroup` at line 41 is elaborated under that variable line, and the file's only `CompleteSpace` binder is now the local one at line 360.
findings.fix: Say "on a normed space `X`" and note that the C₀-semigroup theory proper (uniform boundedness, continuity of orbits at positive times) additionally needs `X` complete.
findings.issue: Docstring says "A strongly continuous one-parameter semigroup (C₀-semigroup) on a Banach space", but after the diff's change to line 35 the structure assumes only [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]. The doc now names a completeness hypothesis the definition does not carry.

findings.evidence: Lines 358-360 add the section with no accompanying prose; the only place Banach-Steinhaus is named is the private helper docstring at line 300 and the `banach_steinhaus` application at line 369, neither of which is visible from the public theorem's documentation.
findings.fix: Add a `/-! ## Results requiring completeness -/` comment (or one line in the section) stating that uniform boundedness on `[0, 1]` comes from Banach-Steinhaus and therefore needs `X` complete, and that left-continuity of orbits follows from it.
findings.issue: `section CompleteSpace` / `variable [CompleteSpace X]` is introduced with no comment on what completeness buys; `normBoundedOnUnitInterval` (line 362) is described as "strong continuity implies uniform boundedness on compact intervals" without mentioning that it rests on Banach-Steinhaus and hence on completeness of `X`.

summary: Removing [CompleteSpace X] from the file-level variable line leaves the StronglyContinuousSemigroup docstring claiming the structure lives "on a Banach space", which is no longer true of its hypotheses. The new completeness section also documents nothing about why completeness is needed.
